title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction: The setting is a ring A all of whose residue characteristics equal a single prime p>0, so effectively A is a Z_(p)-algebra and integers prime to p are units. Take an ideal I with a divided-power structure (pi_n)_{n>=0}; we would now write gamma_n. The goal is to show that the whole PD structure is determined by the single map pi_p : I -> I. (a) The axiom pi_m(x)pi_n(x) = C(m+n,n) pi_{m+n}(x) is the starting point. Suppose m is divisible by p and 1<=n<=p-1. Then C(m+n,n) = prod_{k=1}^n (m+k)/k, and each factor m+k is congruent to k mod p, hence prime to p. So the binomial coefficient is a p-adic unit and pi_{m+n}(x) = C(m+n,n)^{-1} pi_m(x) pi_n(x) (the boxed formula). (b) The composition axiom is pi_m(pi_n(x)) = (mn)!/((n!)^m m!) pi_{mn}(x). - Case m=p: the coefficient is c_n = (pn)!/((n!)^p p!). By Legendre's formula v_p(N!) = (N - s_p(N))/(p-1), and since s_p(pn) = s_p(n), one gets v_p(c_n) = s_p(n) - 1. This is not a unit in general, so this composition is useless for inversion. This bracketed computation is an abandoned attempt. - Case n=p: the coefficient is d_m = (pm)!/((p!)^m m!), and v_p(d_m) = (pm - s)/(p-1) - m - (m - s)/(p-1) = 0. So d_m is a unit and pi_{pm}(x) = d_m^{-1} pi_m(pi_p(x)). Conclusion: (a) and (b) together determine every pi_n from pi_p, by induction on n. - For n
errors: No mathematical errors. Minor point: 'residue characteristics positive' should be read as 'all residue characteristics equal to the same p', i.e. A is a Z_(p)-algebra; otherwise primes other than p need not be invertible and the inversions fail.
In the line v_p(c_n) = Sigma a_i - 1, a factor (written as 1/(p-1) or similar) is crossed out; the final value s_p(n)-1 is correct.
The bracketed m=p computation is a dead end (non-unit coefficient), correctly abandoned in favour of the n=p case.

ideas.what: In a Z_(p)-algebra, a PD structure is determined by gamma_p: gamma_{pm} = unit * gamma_m(gamma_p), and gamma_{pm+r} = unit * gamma_{pm} gamma_r
ideas.modern_name: Determination of divided powers by gamma_p in Z_(p)-algebras; gamma_n(x) = unit * x^{a_0} gamma_p(x)^{a_1} gamma_p(gamma_p(x))^{a_2}...
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard lemma in Berthelot's Cohomologie cristalline (1974, Ch. I) and Berthelot–Ogus Notes on Crystalline Cohomology (1978); roots in Roby/Cartier
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as far as known; possibly implicit in Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (IHES notes, 1966/68)

ideas.what: p-adic valuation computation of the PD composition coefficients (mn)!/((n!)^m m!) via Legendre's formula

deep.surprise_reason: A correct, routine foundational lemma on divided powers in mixed/positive characteristic, well established in Berthelot's thesis and Berthelot–Ogus. It is only of mild historical interest as a trace of Grothendieck working through PD foundations himself.
transcription_corrections: Second line: the object written '(X^{(m)})^{(n)}' is heavily struck out and illegible; the intended content is just 'système de puissances divisées (pi_n)_{n>=0}'.
Superscripts on pi in (a) are struck-out attempts (e.g. pi^{(m)}(x)); the clean reading is pi_m(x)pi_n(x) = C(m+n,n) pi_{m+n}(x).
The condition reads '1 <= n <= p-1' (written '1<=n<=p-1'); 'not ≡ 0 (p)' after the binomial expression is correct (partly struck).
In (b) the composition is pi_m ∘ pi_n with coefficient (mn)!/((n!)^m m!) and pi_{mn} (superscripts struck).
Final displayed formula: pi_{pm} = ((pm)!/((p!)^m m!))^{-1} pi_m ∘ pi_p.
Final line: 'a) et b) ensemble nous montrent que les pi_n sont connus quand on connaît pi_p' (underlined).
